title: Restaurant & Retail Painting in Gainesville & Ocala

sections.h2: Two very different spaces in one building
body: A restaurant is really two jobs. The dining room is a design space: it has to look intentional under evening lighting, match the brand, and feel fresh to guests. The back of house is a working space that gets hit with grease, steam, degreasers, and carts all day. Restaurant and retail painting means treating those as separate systems and pricing them that way.

Retail stores are simpler in materials but harder on time. A sales floor can usually be closed for a few hours, not a few days. We plan every retail and restaurant job around your hours first and pick fast-recoat coatings that fit inside them, so customers never walk into wet walls.

Dining rooms are usually painted overnight, after the last table and before the morning prep shift. Booths and tables are covered or moved, decor comes down and is labeled, and light fixtures and windows are masked. Feature walls, wainscoting, and decorative finishes can be added; we offer decorative and faux finishes like limewash and venetian plaster for spaces that want more character than flat color.

On sales floors, fixtures and displays are moved, masked, and reset. Work is staged after close: tape and mask, spray or roll, and have fixtures back in place and floors clean before the doors open. Fitting rooms, restrooms, and stockrooms can be done in the same pass, and back-office walls can be scheduled for a quieter weeknight.

sections.h2: Back-of-house coatings that can be washed
body: Kitchen, prep, and dish areas need coatings built for constant cleaning. Standard wall paint softens and stains under grease and degreaser. We specify washable, high-performance waterborne or epoxy coatings for those walls, chosen for the specific surface, whether it is painted drywall, block, or existing enamel. Prep starts with degreasing, because any coating over grease will peel where it is hit most.
Concrete and block in storage rooms, walk-in surrounds, and loading areas can be coated through our concrete and masonry painting service.
bullets: Degrease and rinse all walls before prep
Repair dings and gouges from carts and racks
Prime with a product suited to the existing surface
Apply a washable, high-performance finish coat system
Schedule around prep shifts, deliveries, and inspections

sections.h2: Planning a turn around your hours
body: Before we price a retail or restaurant job, we walk the space with the manager and note closing and opening times, delivery windows, prep shifts, alarm procedures, and anything that cannot be moved, like built-in booths, refrigerated cases, or fixed displays. From that we set a night-by-night plan. A small cafe dining room might be one night. A full store with a sales floor, fitting rooms, and stockroom might be several nights in zones, with the most visible areas finished first.

Fast-recoat coatings matter here. Products are chosen so the second coat can go on the same night and the space can open the next day without tacky walls or lingering odor. Each morning the space is clean, the floors are swept, and fixtures and decor are back where they belong. If something is not finished, the area is closed neatly rather than left looking like a job site in front of customers.

Shopping center tenants have one more layer: landlord rules. Many centers require a certificate of insurance, specific work hours, and approval for anything visible from the parking lot. We handle that paperwork as part of the job.

Chains and franchises have brand standards, and independent shops have colors their customers recognize. We match brand colors precisely and record the formula, product, and sheen for every surface, so a touch-up two years later or a second location matches the first. If you are rebranding, a color consultation can help translate a logo palette into wall colors that look right at full scale.

The storefront is often the first thing customers judge. Facades, entry doors, trim, and canopies are covered by our commercial exterior painting service, with entries kept open during the work. Lower walls in high-traffic areas can get an anti-graffiti coating so tagging cleans off without repainting.

For interior work in non-food spaces, see commercial interior painting. We provide a certificate of insurance before mobilization, and you sign off on a final punch walk before the job is closed. Local details are on our Ocala commercial painting page.

faqs.q: Can you paint a restaurant without closing?
faqs.a: Yes. Dining rooms are usually painted overnight between closing and the morning prep shift, and kitchens are scheduled around prep and delivery times.

faqs.q: What paint holds up in a commercial kitchen?
faqs.a: Washable high-performance waterborne or epoxy coatings applied over degreased, properly primed walls. Standard wall paint softens and stains under grease and cleaning chemicals.

faqs.q: How do you match our brand colors exactly?
faqs.a: We match from your brand standards or an existing painted surface and record the formula, product, and sheen so future touch-ups and other locations match.

faqs.q: Do you paint storefront exteriors too?
faqs.a: Yes. Facades, doors, trim, and canopies are handled through our commercial exterior service, with entries kept open during the work.
